dossier.architecture: Protected collector and one pivoting shooter handle speaker/amp; pneumatic zero-time chain climb.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve motor orientation widens the under-bumper intake.
subsystems.intake: Under-bumper urethane rollers and lateral rollers protect pickup hardware inside the perimeter.
subsystems.transfer: Sushi rollers feed directly into the launcher; double-sided belts simplify opposing rotations.
subsystems.scoring: Top/bottom launcher on a high-travel pivot; team reports tuned compression and high release poses against tall defenders.
subsystems.endgame: Pneumatic hooks are supported while enabled and drop as power ends; separate hook positions accommodate solo or partner climbs.
subsystems.controls: Note detection, tag-relative aiming, single-driver controls and tactile/LED readiness signals.

versions: Pre-provincials interview emphasizes autonomous refinement; later binder and Worlds interview must be consulted for final details.
dossier.analysis: Compare endgame time cost against scoring opportunity. The climber's pneumatic capacity and disable behavior are enabling details; a generic hook is not an equivalent architecture.
limits: Configuration description is tied to the cited interview; not a claim that every unreported shop revision is known.
dossier.deep_context:
# 2024-2056: technical mechanisms, design reasoning and revision boundaries

These notes distinguish published construction from team-stated intent and original engineering inference. Selected numerical values are reported source data, not independently reproduced measurements. The recommended tests have not been performed. A binder snapshot does not certify every competition version.

## OPR 2024: chassis and module geometry create the intake path

Version: 2024 pivoting shooter. [PDF p4](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=4) · [PDF p6](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=6) · [PDF p8](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=8)

**Published construction:** Modified front module clearance; under-bumper conveyor; post-Newmarket aluminum side plates and added bracing.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Wide pickup, consistent centering and impact rigidity.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** An under-bumper path consumes the same volume as frame rails and module motors, so module orientation and mounting plates are part of the intake design. Increasing plate rigidity preserves compression but can transmit more collision load elsewhere. The documented event boundary should be retained: the stronger side plates and bracing were a precautionary update rather than necessarily the initial robot. Intake width is useful only if the full path can move off-center notes without trapping them at a module or frame corner.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Test side pickup and corner impacts, then compare roller alignment and chassis squareness before and after the update.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## OPR 2024: pre-compression, differential spin and revised release angle

Version: 2024 pivoting shooter. [PDF p11](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=11) · [PDF p13](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=13) · [PDF p14](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=14)

**Published construction:** Pre-compression contacts, independent left/right drives, low-backlash pivot; flywheels later tipped down 6°.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Consistent feed and greater useful shot range.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A flexible note can enter the same nominal wheel gap in different shapes. Pre-compression aims to control that shape before final acceleration. Independent side speeds then create spin, while mechanically linked upper/lower contacts preserve another aspect of consistency. A six-degree structural change alters the reachable trajectory envelope even if the control software is unchanged. Distinguish output speed, compression and release geometry when diagnosing misses: increasing RPM cannot necessarily compensate for a deformed or inconsistently presented note.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Compare shot distributions before and after the geometric revision with the same notes, recording entry deformation and wheel recovery.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## OPR 2024: pneumatic lift and an explicitly different disable behavior

Version: 2024 pivoting shooter. [PDF p16](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=16)

**Published construction:** Dual pneumatic cylinders and revised double hook; single-acting valve retracts on loss of power.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Fast hanging and compatibility with a partner-loaded chain.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A pneumatic climber stores energy before the lift, reducing the need for a large electric winch during the final action. Available force depends on regulated pressure, piston area and the retracting-side rod area, while repeated actions consume finite stored air. The hook geometry must accommodate a chain already displaced by a partner. The described valve behavior is specific to this plumbing and control configuration; it should not become a generic assumption about all solenoids or an instruction to rely on an untested after-buzzer action.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Test force and timing at the lowest expected pressure, including partner chain displacement and the actual disabled valve state.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## OPR 2024: adapt autonomous to whether a note is actually present

Version: 2024 pivoting shooter. [PDF p20](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=20)

**Published construction:** Game-piece camera, drive-to-point correction, missing-note diversion and velocity-compensated aiming.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Avoid wasting autonomous time on absent or displaced notes.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** An intake with a large acquisition envelope becomes more useful when the path can correct toward the observed note. The controller must decide early enough that a failed attempt does not consume the rest of autonomous. A missing-note branch is a strategy choice tied to contested supply and partner routes, not simply a vision feature. The shot system also depends on current robot velocity and a stable angle reference. Database recommendations should include these feedback assumptions alongside the mechanical pickup.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Displace or remove expected notes and test diversion timing, partner-route safety and the resulting end pose.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## Selected published parameters

| Component | Source parameter | Locator |
|---|---|---|
| Intake | ~1/8-in carpet compression; ~1/4-in conveyor compression | [Source p8](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=8) |
| Pivot | ~107:1 overall | [Source p11](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=11) |
| Shooter | 5/8-in launch compression; team lists left/right 8000/4000 RPM | [Source p14](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=14) |
| Climb | two 1.5-in-bore, 10-in-stroke cylinders; reported ~200-lbf combined retraction | [Source p16](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=16) |

Ratios preserve source notation; verify driver/driven order, complete geometry and the actual version in CAD before fabrication. Figure records retain PDF page and crop bounds in `data/mechanism_images.jsonl`. Images may include rejected prototypes or whole-robot photographs; their captions preserve that distinction.

binder_audit.interpretation: A missing verified binder is an unresolved retrieval result, not evidence the team never published one. Existing interviews/CAD sources remain usable.

source_reviews.title: OP Robotics 2024 Crescendo Technical Binder
source_reviews.locator: Drivetrain, Swerve Module, Intake, Frame and Tower, Shoulder Gearbox, Shooter and Climber
facts: Front MK4i modules are modified to clear the note and carry kicker mounts. One motor drives opposed intake rows through a gearbox and belts.
The note passes under a solid front steel bar. The tower carries a dead-axle shooter pivot and low-backlash shoulder drive.
Post-Newmarket changes include braced aluminum intake plates, a rear reinforcement and revised flywheels and hooks.
source_reviews.limitations: Published values and intentions belong to the binder configuration. Full tolerance, maintenance and installation records are absent.

source_reviews.title: LOW-KEY binder and drawing release
facts: Team identifies the 2024 robot as LOW-KEY and publishes binder and drawing package.
source_reviews.limitations: No drawing dimensions derived in this pass.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: LOW-KEY is built around a low protected note path and a variable-angle scorer. The front end is one mechanism in practice even though its parts belong to the chassis, swerve and collector. A front bar leaves the ring a passage beneath it. Modified drive modules clear that passage and carry nearby intake hardware. A fixed tower supports a compact launcher that both receives and aims the note. The team's choice to pursue low pivot backlash made the structure and gearbox part of the shot-angle measurement system.
piece_flow: The front roller pinches a floor note against carpet. Opposed linked rollers move it upward and toward the center.
Belts carry motion between conveyor shafts and help guide the note between roller pairs. An intake photoeye supports automation.
The scorer receives the note on small feed rollers, applies side pre-compression and accelerates it through independent left/right flywheel pairs. Shoulder pitch also enables amp geometry.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: Keep the note corridor drawn alongside the wheel and gear envelopes. The inverted front module motor and modified bottom plate are local accommodations for that corridor. A cover keeps notes out of the electronics bay. The pivot support is a fixed tower axle, which gives a defined load path from shooter to frame. In a copy, the shoulder transmission and tower together determine whether a motor encoder reflects true exit angle during acceleration.

subsystems.name: Integrated front intake
subsystems.construction: Steel front member, aluminum frame, modified swerve mounts and multi-roller pickup driven by a Kraken through belts and a reversing gearbox.
subsystems.operation: Pinch the note, center it and move it up the conveyor under the front of the chassis.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team wanted a protected intake with forgiving perimeter and open-field pickup, plus centered shooter delivery.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The front module is a note-path part. A nominally equivalent swerve replacement can put a motor or fastener in the capture corridor. Wide contact only buys useful acquisition if both edges hand off reliably.
subsystems.interfaces: Carpet, bumper opening, steel crossmember, corner module and kicker mounts.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: After an impact, measure the mouth and conveyor nip at both sides. Confirm a replacement module preserves the passage before re-enabling automated pickup.
subsystems.unknowns: Measured capture distribution and post-impact datums.

subsystems.name: Shoulder, shooter and feed
subsystems.construction: Bronze bushings around a dead axle, bonded gears and custom broached sprockets. Feed and passive pre-compression rollers lead to independent side flywheels.
subsystems.operation: Set the pitch and feed the note into a repeatable compressed state before launch.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team sought small backlash during motion and shots so it could use motor encoder feedback. Side speed differences apply spin.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The reported radial pre-compression and flywheel nip act in different directions. A damaged ring can retain asymmetry into the shot. Under load, elastic deflection can remain even when free backlash is small.
subsystems.interfaces: Frame stiffness, shoulder mesh and launch readiness interact with note centering.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Measure physical exit angle under acceleration and torque reversal. Track angle after chain adjustment and after a representative hit.
subsystems.unknowns: Shot dispersion, long-term gear fit and actual angular compliance.

subsystems.name: Climber
subsystems.construction: Binder documents a double hook actuated by two pneumatic cylinders, with extension flow management and integrated camera mounting.
subsystems.operation: Reach the chain and retract to load it. The revised hook accommodates a chain already pulled down by a partner.
subsystems.team_rationale: Fast reliable engagement and partner clearance were requirements.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The chain geometry can inform an electric design. Retraction force and holding behavior must be sized for that new actuator and evaluated across full stroke.
subsystems.interfaces: Hooks, cylinders, frame brackets and note-camera mount share space.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect one-sided loading and retention. Verify electrical actuation separately if transferring the reach geometry.
subsystems.unknowns: Measured impact loads and actual match-by-match climb outcome.

revisions: Binder explicitly marks post-Newmarket reinforcements, flywheel change and double-hook update.
transferable_principles: Make the note corridor an explicit chassis interface. Qualify true loaded pivot angle before relying on motor feedback alone.
disconfirming_conditions: The integrated front package is a poor copy if module swaps alter the throat or field-contact deflection consumes the floor gap. The published pneumatic drive is outside the workspace's electric-actuation scope.
remaining_gaps: Exact event revisions, logged shot and climb data, dimensional inspection of front intake interfaces.
